content: Phenobarbital reduces the plasma levels or therapeutic effects of itraconazole by enhancing P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter activity. Exercise caution and monitor closely. Phenobarbital decreases the levels or effects of ivermectin through P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter modulation. Use caution and monitor. Phenobarbital reduces the levels or efficacy of ixabepilone by inducing hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 enzyme metabolism. Caution and monitoring are advised. Ixekizumab may normalize CYP450 enzyme formation altered by elevated cytokine levels during chronic inflammation. When initiating or discontinuing ixekizumab in patients on concomitant CYP450 substrates, particularly those with a narrow therapeutic index, monitor therapeutic effects closely. Kava enhances the effects of phenobarbital via pharmacodynamic synergism, potentially increasing CNS depression. Use caution and monitor. Ketamine and phenobarbital both increase sedation. Caution and monitoring are necessary. Phenobarbital and ketotifen (ophthalmic) both enhance sedative effects. Use caution and monitor. Phenobarbital reduces labetalol levels by increasing its metabolism. Consider a higher beta-blocker dose during coadministration. Atenolol, sotalol, and nadolol are less likely to be affected. Phenobarbital decreases lamotrigine levels by enhancing hepatic clearance. Use caution and monitor. Phenobarbital reduces lansoprazole levels or effects by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are recommended. Phenobarbital decreases lapatinib levels or effects by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism and enhancing P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter activity. Use caution and monitor. Lasmiditan and phenobarbital both increase sedation. Coadministration with other CNS depressants, including alcohol, has not been clinically evaluated. Lasmiditan may cause sedation and other cognitive or neuropsychiatric adverse effects. Use caution and monitor. Lemborexant and phenobarbital both enhance sedative effects. Dosage adjustments may be necessary when lemborexant is coadministered with other CNS depressants due to additive effects. Modify therapy and monitor closely. Phenobarbital reduces lesinurad levels or effects by inducing CYP2C9/10 metabolism. Modify therapy and monitor closely. Phenobarbital increases sedation, while levalbuterol decreases it. The interaction effect is unclear; use caution and monitor. Phenobarbital reduces levamlodipine levels or effects by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. No quantitative data on CYP3A4 inducers' effects on amlodipine are available. Monitor blood pressure closely when coadministered with CYP3A4 inducers. Levocetirizine and phenobarbital both increase sedation. Use caution and monitor. Phenobarbital decreases levonorgestrel levels (intrauterine and oral) by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Hormonal contraceptive efficacy may be reduced. Use alternative or backup contraception during enzyme inducer use and for 28 days after discontinuation. Phenobarbital and levorphanol both increase sedation. Use caution and monitor. Phenobarbital reduces lidocaine levels or effects by inducing CYP1A2 metabolism. Use caution and monitor. Phenobarbital decreases linagliptin levels or effects by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Alternative treatments are strongly recommended when linagliptin is coadministered with a CYP3A4 inducer. Phenobarbital increases sedation, while lisdexamfetamine decreases it. The interaction effect is unclear; use caution and monitor. Belladonna alkaloids and lofepramine both decrease cholinergic effects. Phenobarbital and lofepramine both increase sedation. Use caution and monitor. Phenobarbital and lofexidine both enhance sedative effects. Use caution and monitor. Belladonna alkaloids reduce loxapine levels by inhibiting gastrointestinal absorption. This applies only to oral forms. Belladonna alkaloids also decrease loxapine levels via pharmacodynamic antagonism, while loxapine increases belladonna alkaloid effects through pharmacodynamic synergism. Use caution and monitor. Lonapegsomatropin decreases phenobarbital levels or effects by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Limited data suggest growth hormone treatment increases CYP450-mediated clearance. Use caution with sensitive CYP substrates. Phenobarbital reduces loperamide levels or effects by enhancing P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter activity. Use caution and monitor. Phenobarbital decreases lopinavir levels or effects by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor. Phenobarbital and loprazolam both increase sedation. Use caution and monitor. Phenobarbital reduces loratadine levels or effects by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Both loratadine and phenobarbital increase sedation. Use caution and monitor. Phenobarbital and lorazepam both enhance sedative effects. Use caution and monitor. Phenobarbital and lormetazepam both increase sedation. Use caution and monitor. Phenobarbital reduces losartan levels or effects by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor. Phenobarbital decreases lovastatin levels or effects by enhancing P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter activity. Use caution and monitor. Phenobarbital and loxapine both increase sedation. Use caution and monitor. Phenobarbital and loxapine inhaled both enhance sedative effects. Loxapine inhaled increases belladonna alkaloid effects via pharmacodynamic synergism, while belladonna alkaloids reduce loxapine inhaled levels through pharmacodynamic antagonism. Use caution and monitor. Lumacaftor/ivacaftor and phenobarbital interact by affecting CYP2C19 metabolism. In vitro studies suggest lumacaftor induces and ivacaftor inhibits CYP2C19 substrates. Use caution and monitor. Belladonna alkaloids and maprotiline both decrease cholinergic effects. Use caution and monitor. Lumateperone and phenobarbital both increase sedation. Use caution and monitor. Lurasidone and phenobarbital both enhance sedation and may increase each other's toxicity. Use caution and monitor. Phenobarbital and maprotiline both increase sedation. Use caution and monitor. Phenobarbital reduces maraviroc levels or effects by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism and enhancing P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter activity. Use caution and monitor. Phenobarbital and marijuana both increase sedation. Phenobarbital reduces marijuana levels or effects by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor. Meclizine and phenobarbital both enhance sedative effects. Belladonna alkaloids and meclizine both decrease cholinergic effects. Use caution and monitor. Phenobarbital reduces medroxyprogesterone levels or effects by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Contraceptive failure is possible. Modify therapy and monitor closely. Belladonna alkaloids and methscopolamine both decrease cholinergic effects. Use caution and monitor. Phenobarbital and mefloquine interact by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism, potentially reducing each other's effects. Use caution and monitor. Phenobarbital and melatonin both increase sedation. Phenobarbital reduces melatonin levels or effects by inducing CYP1A2 metabolism. Use caution and monitor. Phenobarbital and meperidine both enhance sedative effects. Use caution and monitor. Phenobarbital and meprobamate both increase sedation. Use caution and monitor. Phenobarbital reduces mestranol levels or effects by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism and enhancing P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter activity. Use caution and monitor. Phenobarbital increases sedation, while metaproterenol decreases it. The interaction effect is unclear; use caution and monitor. Phenobarbital and metaxalone both enhance sedative effects. Use caution and monitor. Phenobarbital reduces methadone levels or effects by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Both phenobarbital and methadone increase sedation. Use caution and monitor. Phenobarbital increases sedation, while methamphetamine decreases it. The interaction effect is unclear; use caution and monitor. Phenobarbital and methocarbamol both enhance sedative effects. Use caution and monitor. Methsuximide and phenobarbital both increase sedation. Use caution and monitor. Phenobarbital increases sedation, while methylenedioxymethamphetamine decreases it. The interaction effect is unclear; use caution and monitor. Methylphenidate increases phenobarbital levels or effects by an unknown mechanism. Monitor for increased serum concentrations or toxicity of phenobarbital when methylphenidate is initiated or its dose is increased, and for decreased concentrations or effects when methylphenidate is discontinued or its dose is reduced. Methylphenidate transdermal increases phenobarbital levels or effects by reducing metabolism. Consider dose adjustments and monitor closely for drug toxicities when initiating or discontinuing methylphenidate. Phenobarbital reduces methylprednisolone levels or effects by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism and enhancing P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter activity. Use caution and monitor. Phenobarbital decreases metoprolol levels by increasing its metabolism. Consider a higher beta-blocker dose during coadministration. Atenolol, sotalol, and nadolol are less likely to be affected. Phenobarbital reduces mexiletine levels or effects by inducing CYP1A2 metabolism. Use caution and monitor. Phenobarbital reduces midazolam levels or effects by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Both phenobarbital and midazolam increase sedation. Use caution and monitor. Midazolam intranasal and phenobarbital may increase each other's toxicity via pharmacodynamic synergism. Concomitant use of barbiturates, alcohol, or other CNS depressants may increase the risk of hypoventilation, airway obstruction, desaturation, or apnea, contributing to profound and/or prolonged drug effects. Modify therapy and monitor closely. Phenobarbital increases sedation, while midodrine decreases it. The interaction effect is unclear; use caution and monitor. Phenobarbital reduces mifepristone levels or effects by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. CYP3A4 inducers have not been studied; coadministration is not recommended by the manufacturer. Mipomersen and phenobarbital may increase each other's toxicity. Both drugs have the potential to elevate hepatic enzymes; monitor liver function tests (LFTs). Use caution and monitor. Phenobarbital and mirtazapine both enhance sedative effects. Phenobarbital reduces mirtazapine levels or effects by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor. Phenobarbital increases sedation, while modafinil decreases it. The interaction effect is unclear; use caution and monitor. Molindone and phenobarbital both enhance sedative effects. Use caution and monitor. Phenobarbital and morphine both increase sedation. Use caution and monitor. Phenobarbital and motherwort both enhance sedative effects. Use caution and monitor. Phenobarbital and moxonidine both increase sedation. Use caution and monitor. Phenobarbital and nabilone both enhance sedative effects. Use caution and monitor. Phenobarbital reduces nadolol levels by increasing its metabolism. Consider a higher beta-blocker dose during coadministration. Atenolol, sotalol, and nadolol are less likely to be affected. Phenobarbital and nalbuphine both enhance sedative effects. Use caution and monitor. Phenobarbital reduces nateglinide levels or effects by inducing CYP2C9/10 metabolism. Use caution and monitor. Phenobarbital decreases nebivolol levels by increasing its metabolism. Consider a higher beta-blocker dose during coadministration. Atenolol, sotalol, and nadolol are less likely to be affected. Phenobarbital reduces nefazodone levels or effects by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor. Phenobarbital reduces nelfinavir levels or effects by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism and enhancing P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter activity. Use caution and monitor. Phenobarbital reduces neomycin PO levels or effects by enhancing P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter activity. Use caution and monitor. Neostigmine increases cholinergic effects, while belladonna alkaloids decrease them. The interaction effect is unclear; use caution and monitor. Phenobarbital and nevirapine interact by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism, potentially reducing each other's effects. Use caution and monitor. Phenobarbital reduces nicardipine levels or effects by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor. Phenobarbital reduces nifedipine levels or effects by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Modify therapy and monitor closely.
